# Twenty-Four Cousins

> A field guide to the human family in one page, by Curtis Hoffmann: twenty-four hominin species across seven million years, with a time slider, a species timeline, a brain-size chart, a trait grid, a side-by-side comparison tool, and a sourced profile for every species.

Site: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/
Source and data (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 dataset): https://github.com/phagehunter/humanevolution

## Main sections (one page, anchored)

- Time slider, seven million years to the present: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#scrub
- Timeline, every species as a bar, oldest first: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#timeline
- Brain size against time for the 22 species with a measurable skull: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#brains
- Trait grid (bipedalism, feet, hands, hip, posture, jaw, brow ridge, prognathism, diet, tools): https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#traits
- Compare any two species: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#compare
- Species profiles, each with a permanent link, for example https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#homo-naledi : https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#species
- Where the numbers come from: https://curtishoffmann.com/humanevolution/#sources

## Data

- Dataset: `data/species.json` in the repository, 24 species with time range, cranial capacity, stature, discovery year and site, type site, naming status, and a note and source for each value. Compiled 14 October 2026.
- Quantitative values: Smithsonian Human Origins Program species pages; Australian Museum human-evolution pages; primary papers where those are silent (Lebatard et al. 2008, Ferring et al. 2011, Lordkipanidze et al. 2007 and 2013, Grün et al. 2020).
- Qualitative trait descriptors and the species list: the Kaggle teaching dataset "Biological Data of Human Ancestors" (santiago123678). They are categorical summaries, not measurements.
- Caveat: twenty-four is the Kaggle list, not a verdict on how many hominin species existed. Homo georgicus and Homo rhodesiensis are often folded into Homo erectus and Homo heidelbergensis; Ardipithecus kadabba, Kenyanthropus platyops, Homo luzonensis and the Denisovans are absent.
